source.title: Detecting overfitting in Neural Networks during long-horizon grokking using Random Matrix Theory

record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly describes reproducing known grokking experiments and reports train/test accuracy trajectories, while extending them to long-horizon training.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own train/test accuracy outcomes on grokking benchmarks and an MNIST MLP, plus a weight-decay comparison. Correlation Trap counts, localization analyses, and JSD trap-ablation results are not rows for versions that name delayed generalization, circuit formation, or optimizer artifacts; they do not directly measure those claims. The paper does not vary training-set size.
record.test_reason: The paper reproduces known grokking setups only as a testbed for its weight-only Correlation Trap diagnostic. These are the Liu et al.-style MNIST MLP with 8x init scale, modular addition, and Wang et al.'s GPT2 composition task. Phases are 'descriptive phase labels tied to the observed train/test trajectories', so the phase-sliced accuracies cannot independently test V1. Training-set size, initialization scale, circuits, optimizer or precision artifacts, and dataset size for ungrokking are never varied. Its new empirical result, post-grokking test-accuracy decline ('anti-grokking'), is not something any version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it omits the main conclusion. The authors' central claim is that Correlation Traps (MP-edge outliers in entry-shuffled weight spectra) appear only in anti-grokking, not in pre-grokking or grokking, and can detect harmful overfitting from weights alone. A JSD ablation test distinguishes harmful from benign traps, and gpt-oss models show many traps. The weight-decay reduction of degradation is a secondary control.
record.recipe_differences: Uses grokking-style training and train/test accuracy trajectories, but studies MNIST, modular addition, and synthetic composition with extended long-horizon runs; the main contribution is a shuffled-spectrum diagnostic rather than a training-set-size study.
record.method_sensitivity: The MLP comparison shows that WD=0.01 reduces trap growth and late-stage test degradation relative to WD=0. The paper also reports that the exact anti-grokking onset varies modestly across seeds, while its qualitative phase ordering remains.

fits_no_version.finding: After grokking, long-horizon training without weight decay makes test accuracy decline while train accuracy stays at 1.0. MA test accuracy goes from 0.97 to 0.68; the MNIST MLP and GPT2 also drop substantially. WD=0.01 reduces but does not remove the decline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anti-grokking: grokked solutions can be lost under continued optimization (post-generalization overfitting), and weight decay mitigates this.

fits_no_version.finding: Shuffled-spectrum outliers (Correlation Traps) are zero in pre-grok and grok phases and appear only in anti-grokking. Examples: MA mean 4.88 ± 1.55 traps per layer; MLP FC1 7.5 ± 5.6 at WD=0 vs 2.0 at WD>0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A weight-only spectral diagnostic separates post-grokking overfitting from pre-grokking memorization.

record.code_released: https://github.com/CalculatedContent/WeightWatcher; the paper also describes a supplemental artifact bundle but gives no URL for it.
record.problems: The paper does not vary training-set size, and does not give a chance-accuracy baseline for the reported pre-grok MA result. Several plotted accuracy values are not stated numerically in the text. Evidence is limited to three controlled grokking settings; the authors also describe the robustness summaries qualitatively.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size; test accuracy at chance before the jump. The setups are reproductions, not tests.
Switching the delay on or off via initialization scale or weight norm. The MNIST run uses a fixed 8x init and never varies it.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, ungrokking.
Not addressed; no circuit or progress-measure analysis bearing on the grokking transition.
Not addressed. The MLP is trained in float64 with AdamW, but neither optimizer nor precision is varied.

record.verdict_notes: The MNIST MLP uses parameters scaled by 8.0 at initialization, the Omnigrok recipe. This is relevant to V3 but is not varied, so it offers no evidence on the lazy-to-rich switch. Phase boundaries differ between experiments; for example, the Appendix C perturbation study redefines them. Seed robustness is reported only qualitatively (Table 13). The paper is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The effect of training-set size on the delay is not tested. The paper does not state a chance-accuracy baseline for the pre-grokging result.

The paper does not sweep initialization scale or test a lazy-to-rich transition. The weight-decay comparison concerns late-stage degradation, not whether norm or initialization switches the grokking delay on or off.
The paper does not test whether weight decay selects a more efficient generalizing circuit, nor a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.

relation.reason: The study uses induced grokking trajectories to evaluate an overfitting diagnostic; it does not independently test the listed claim versions.

tranche.reason: Known grokking setups are deliberately reproduced as a testbed for the Correlation Trap diagnostic. The checked results concern subsequent degradation and its mitigation, which no listed claim version names.

source_check.notes: Anti-grokking is post-generalization degradation, distinct from delayed generalization and dataset-reduction ungrokking. GPT2 uses synthetic composition data; the foundation-model screening does not demonstrate grokking.

statements.correction: Modular addition, Table 4: Grok test accuracy 0.97 ± 0.02; Anti-grok test accuracy 0.68 ± 0.11; train accuracy 1.0 ± 0.0 in both phases; statistics across sampled checkpoints. Modular-addition weight decay: not stated. MNIST MLP, Section 5.3 and Appendix A.2: WD=0.01 reduces late-stage test degradation relative to WD=0 without eliminating overfitting.
statements.problem: The accuracy numbers correctly describe modular addition, but its weight decay is not stated. The WD=0 versus WD=0.01 comparison concerns the MNIST MLP. The modular-addition numbers are phase means, not individual trajectory endpoints.
